standard: TEKS 8.10 — how the Erie Canal's waterway and transportation drove regional economic development in the early 19th century
frame: A multi-year public-works project the player oversees and manages across years and setbacks. This is NOT a journey, NOT a trail, NOT a survival trek. The player does not travel point A to point B.
playerRole: You are the Erie Canal Commission — the body responsible for funding, building, and completing the canal.

cast.name: DeWitt Clinton
cast.significance: This figure demonstrates how political leadership and vision drove the massive public works project that transformed American commerce.
cast.relationshipToPlayer: The player encounters him as the primary advocate securing state funding and political support for the canal construction.

cast.name: Benjamin Wright
cast.significance: This figure represents the technical expertise and engineering innovation required to build the canal through challenging terrain.
cast.relationshipToPlayer: The player works with him to solve construction challenges and implement the engineering solutions that made the canal possible.

cast.name: Irish Canal Laborer (representative)
cast.significance: This figure represents the thousands of immigrant laborers whose dangerous work built the canal and shows the human cost of the project.
cast.relationshipToPlayer: The player manages and coordinates with these workers who perform the actual excavation and construction of the canal.

cast.name: New York City Merchant (representative)
cast.significance: This figure demonstrates how the canal transformed trade routes and created new commercial opportunities that drove economic growth.
cast.relationshipToPlayer: The player encounters them as they adapt their business practices to take advantage of the new water transportation route.

cast.name: Western New York Farmer (representative)
cast.significance: This figure shows how the canal connected rural producers to distant markets and transformed agricultural practices in the region.
cast.relationshipToPlayer: The player works with them to establish new shipping routes and market connections that the canal made possible.

cast.name: Martin Van Buren
cast.significance: This figure represents the political opposition and skepticism the canal project faced, showing the controversy over public spending.
cast.relationshipToPlayer: The player must navigate his objections and political resistance to the canal's funding and construction.

economy.learningObjective: The Erie Canal's success depended on balancing construction costs, labor management, and engineering challenges to create a profitable waterway that transformed regional trade.

resources.name: funding
resources.description: New York State's financial commitment to the canal project, including bonds and tax revenue
resources.raisedBy: Securing legislative appropriations, issuing canal bonds, collecting tolls from completed sections
resources.drainedBy: Construction costs, worker wages, engineering surveys, land acquisition, unexpected geological problems
resources.degradationEffect: Lower funding forces cheaper construction methods, longer work delays, and reduced canal depth or width

resources.name: workforce
resources.description: Available workers including Irish immigrants, local farmers, and skilled engineers
resources.raisedBy: Recruiting immigrant workers, offering competitive wages, establishing work camps, training local laborers
resources.drainedBy: Disease outbreaks, dangerous working conditions, seasonal departures, competition from other projects
resources.degradationEffect: Reduced workforce slows construction progress and forces reliance on less experienced workers

resources.name: engineering
resources.description: Knowledge and innovation needed to solve canal construction challenges
resources.raisedBy: Learning from European canal systems, trial and error problem-solving, developing new techniques, training American engineers
resources.drainedBy: Complex terrain challenges, lock construction difficulties, water level management problems, geological surprises
resources.degradationEffect: Lower expertise leads to construction delays, water leakage, unstable locks, and costly repairs

resources.name: political_support
resources.description: Political backing from legislators, governors, and citizens across New York State
resources.raisedBy: Demonstrating economic benefits, completing successful canal sections, promoting regional development, managing costs effectively
resources.drainedBy: Cost overruns, construction delays, political opposition, competing state priorities, skepticism about benefits
resources.degradationEffect: Weakened support reduces future funding, increases legislative oversight, and threatens project completion

ratingRubric.basis: How well the player understood and managed the real factors that determined the Erie Canal's transformative economic impact

bands.label: Canal Visionary
bands.description: Demonstrated deep understanding that the canal's success required balancing immediate construction challenges with long-term economic transformation, managing resources to create a durable waterway that revolutionized regional trade

bands.label: Competent Engineer
bands.description: Showed solid grasp of canal construction priorities, generally managing workforce and funding effectively while developing adequate engineering solutions for most challenges

bands.label: Struggling Overseer
bands.description: Understood some aspects of canal management but struggled to balance competing demands, resulting in a functional but problematic waterway with limited economic impact

bands.label: Failed Administrator
bands.description: Missed the key dynamics of canal development, focusing on single issues while neglecting the interconnected nature of funding, labor, engineering, and political support needed for transformative infrastructure
